summary.top_priority: Business-critical content is only present after client-side JavaScript execution

findings.title: Business-critical content is only present after client-side JavaScript execution
findings.evidence: http://127.0.0.1:9700/ (HTTP 200) serves only 34 characters (5 words) of extractable body text; the element #root is empty in the raw HTML and is populated at runtime by inline JavaScript carrying 0 characters of markup (0 words) across 0 injection sites. The framework root element carries no server-rendered children.

suggested_action.summary: Server-side render (SSR) or statically pre-render the product, pricing and company sections into the initial HTML response for #root inside <main>, keeping JavaScript for enhancement only, and mirror the same values in Product/Offer JSON-LD structured data. Verify with a text-only fetch (`curl`) that the raw HTML already carries the prices, so the facts are machine-readable for AI crawlers and assistants that never execute JavaScript and can be extracted and cited.
suggested_action.mechanism: Most AI retrieval pipelines index the raw HTTP response; content injected by the browser after load is invisible to them, so JS-only facts are simply absent from the model's evidence.

findings.title: Key business facts cannot be extracted from the HTML by a text-based crawler
findings.evidence: http://127.0.0.1:9700/ (HTTP 200) yields only 34 characters (5 words) of extractable text, and 4 of 4 fact families are absent from it (missing: company_facts, contact, pricing, product_detail). The page advertises 0 fact sections () but supplies no prices, contact details or company figures in HTML text. Root cause measured on this page: client-side rendering.

suggested_action.summary: Publish the product, pricing, company and contact facts as server-rendered HTML text in the initial response - real <h2> headings, paragraphs and tables rather than JavaScript payloads or images - and back them with Organization and Product JSON-LD structured data. Then verify with a text-only fetch: whatever `curl` returns is the machine-readable evidence an AI assistant can extract, quote and cite.
suggested_action.mechanism: Retrieval-augmented assistants chunk and embed the text of the HTTP response. If the response has no facts, the site is either omitted from the answer or represented by a competitor's page that does state them.

recommendations.title: Use server-side rendering or static generation for product and pricing content
recommendations.detail: Beyond the immediate fix, make pre-rendering the default for any route that carries commercial facts: render critical business information into the initial HTML response at build or request time, and treat client-side injection as enhancement only.

recommendations.title: Mirror the JavaScript-rendered facts in Product/Offer structured data
recommendations.detail: Structured data is served in the initial HTML response even when the visible page hydrates later, so publishing the same prices and product names as JSON-LD gives AI systems a machine-readable copy while the rendering work is in progress.

recommendations.title: Re-check navigation once the initial HTML is server-rendered
recommendations.detail: Every crawled page is a JavaScript shell, so navigation landmarks and internal links could not be measured from the HTML response. Fix the rendering gap first, then re-run this audit; crawlers build their link graph from the served HTML, so client-side-only navigation is invisible to them.

recommendations.title: Publish an XML sitemap with lastmod dates
recommendations.detail: No /sitemap.xml was served. A sitemap with accurate <lastmod> values gives crawlers a cheap freshness signal and a complete URL inventory, which improves how quickly new facts are picked up.

recommendations.title: Add an explicit robots.txt that names AI user agents
recommendations.detail: No robots.txt was served. An explicit allow-list for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended documents your intent and prevents defensive bot rules from silently blocking assistants.

recommendations.title: Add Organization schema alongside the existing structured data
recommendations.detail: Structured data is present (SoftwareApplication) but no Organization/LocalBusiness node was found. Organization markup is what ties products, reviews and articles to a single citable entity.

recommendations.title: Validate structured data in CI so a syntax error cannot ship
recommendations.detail: The site already relies on JSON-LD, so a single malformed block silently removes every machine-readable fact on that page. Add a schema validation step to the build (a JSON parse plus a schema.org type check) to keep the markup trustworthy.

recommendations.title: Add FAQPage schema for the questions buyers actually ask
recommendations.detail: FAQ structured data is the cheapest way to get exact question/answer pairs into AI answers, and it reuses copy you already have on product and support pages.
